title: Count direction improved prediction beyond cell biases and one-way wiring in two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether chemical synapse count balance predicts the direction fraction in another adult C. elegans brain map. In 1,163 selected pairs from Witvliet maps 7 and 8, count balance improved a held-out log score by 0.02620 nats per pair after control for cell send-receive biases and one-way wiring. A nominal fixed-prediction neuron-class resampling interval was 0.01115 to 0.04573. The reverse test gave 0.03462. In 149 pairs with both directions in both maps, gains were 0.05130 and 0.05494. Five folds kept neuron-class pairs together. The design was refined after an initial cell-only result. Two animals, selected pairs, restricted cell controls, and no neural activity limit inference. Counts are not physiological weights. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction. External data and record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Count balance improved held-out scores after cell and one-way wiring controls. Intervals use fixed-prediction neuron-class resampling. All tests reuse two animals.

citations.reason: Prior mirror-edge prediction study informed the distinction between presence and direction fraction; no code or tables reused.
